title: The Mystery: Same Brain, Different Apps
text: Hi, I'm Harshita Nimble, a product designer. Today's ask, why do two apps running the exact same AI model feel completely different to use? Here's the shape of it. The model isn't what you're feeling, something else is. Two food delivery apps, same model underneath. One orders with total confidence. One asks first and remembers what you like. The model didn't change, the wrapping around it did. Meet two food delivery

title: App A vs. App B: Food Delivery Comparison
text: Assistants. Same brain underneath, same model, same weights, same training. Now watch what happens when you ask either one to order dinner. App A just places the order. Pepperoni, your usual, charged to your card, no confirmation, no explanation, done in 2 seconds. Fast. Also, if we're honest, a little unsettling. App B asks first. Your usual pepperoni or want to try the new place down the street? It remembers you skipped mushrooms last time.

title: What Is the AI Harness?
text: Slower, but you trust it. Here's the part that surprises people. The model itself never decided any of that. It doesn't know what ask first means. It just generates the most likely next response. Everything you just felt came from somewhere else. That somewhere else is the harness, the code wrapped around the model. It decides four things: what the model is allowed to do, what it's allowed to

title: The 4 Controls: Permissions, Memory, Visibility, Confirmation
text: Remember, how much it shows you, and whether it asks first or just acts. App A, full permission to spend, no memory, no explanation, acts alone. App B, asks before spending, remembers your preferences, shows its reasoning. Same model, four different settings. This is true of every AI product you've ever used, the chatbot, the coding assistant, the email drafter. The model is the engine. The harness is the steering wheel, the brakes, and the dashboard. The model is raw capability.

title: Prompt Exercise: Auditing Your Product's Harness
text: The harness is what people actually trust, and that's the part almost nobody designs on purpose. Your turn. Pick one AI product you use every day and ask Claude, "What is it allowed to do without asking me first? What does it remember about me? And how much of its reasoning does it actually show?" Then ask what would change if the exact same model sat inside a stricter harness. Why two AI apps using the same model feel completely different? I'm Harshita Nimble.
